author: vanaukenk
body:
I'm opening a new ticket in the annotation tracker in response to the discussion in this ontology ticket:

https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/30805

The issue for me started with reviewing the C. elegans genes with 'contributes to' for MF annotation in the context of modeling complexes as enablers in GO-CAMs.

I had questions about the correct term to use for the SDHA/SDH1 subunit of respiratory chain complex II in the context of the respective BPs.  Note: for this question, I'm only refering to the enzymatic activities, not any of the binding activities.

To try to align the C. elegans annotations with what other groups have done, I made a [spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1h0_fUrGRlDKUyy9o1S3gMuN8XiVJW_3vHwIe5aaP250/edit?gid=2133993244#gid=2133993244) of existing annotations for a select few organisms.

Looking over these annotations, the answer isn't clear, even just for standard annotations.  

@ValWood @rozaru @sjm41 @pgaudet @raymond91125
title: Consistency of SDHA/SDH1 MF annotations

author: vanaukenk
source_title: New specific terms to represent the parts of succinate dehydrogenase performed by SDHA and SDHB

author: pgaudet
body:
As far as I understand, the correct annotations are 

https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/30805#issuecomment-4175011970

> SdhA / SdhB / SdhC / SdhD
contributes to succinate dehydrogenase (quinone) activity

individual reactions should not be captured, as they correspond to substeps. 

(@ValWood proposed to capture substeps in order to join models, but we seem to have agreed not to do that).
